clue.text: Tribal conflict involving northern part of UK

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so one piece wraps round the others

blocks.note: N is the standard abbreviation for northern
Northern Ireland, one of the four parts of the United Kingdom, abbreviated
a clash is a fight or conflict

explanation.surface: A news line about a tribal feud breaking out somewhere in the north of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tribal conflict' reads as one phrase, but 'Tribal' alone is the definition. Northern Ireland is the part of the UK outside Great Britain, hence its two-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Clannish describes people who stick closely to their own group or clan, which is a tribal attitude.

clue.text: Mimic law enforcer unknown on twin-hulled vessel

blocks.note: a cop is a police officer
algebra's unknowns are x, y and z
short for catamaran, a boat with two hulls

explanation.surface: A police officer of uncertain identity is shown aboard a catamaran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mimic' looks like a verb but is the noun definition; in a down clue 'on' lets the earlier pieces sit above CAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A copycat is a person who imitates others, so the noun fits a mimic exactly.

clue.text: For treatment, attain old type of drug?

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, describing the type of drug

indicators.note: letters given treatment are worked on and processed into a new form

blocks.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone seeking a cure resolves to obtain an old-fashioned drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For treatment' sounds medical and fits the drug theme, but it is the signal to rearrange the following two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidotal drug is one acting as an antidote, counteracting a poison, so it describes a kind of medicine.

clue.text: State of trap set up on river to the north

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up raises it so it reads from bottom to top
heading north in a down entry means running upward, against the reading direction

blocks.note: a gin is a snare or trap for animals
the Aire is a river in Yorkshire, northern England

explanation.surface: Someone describes the condition of an animal trap placed beside a northern river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State of' reads as 'condition of', but 'State' is a country; both pieces are turned upward and 'on' stacks the first above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigeria is a sovereign nation in West Africa, and state is a common word for a country.

clue.text: Dawn’s salary hike supporting daily

indicators.note: in a down entry, whatever supports another lies underneath it, so it comes second

blocks.note: The Sun is a British daily newspaper
in Britain a pay increase is called a rise

explanation.surface: A woman named Dawn gets a pay increase that helps her daily life.
explanation.walkthrough: Dawn looks like a woman's name. In a down clue, one piece 'supporting' another sits below it, so the newspaper goes on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunrise is the moment the sun appears in the morning, the same time of day as dawn.

clue.text: Blank-looking worker on short holiday

indicators.note: in an across entry, being on something means following it, so the preceding piece is placed second

blocks.note: vac is the British short form of vacation, especially a university holiday
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: An employee on a brief break wears an empty expression.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' simply means placed after, so the insect follows the holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacant expression shows no thought or interest, which is exactly a blank look.

clue.text: Priest originally taking grain round large chamber

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept
to go round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: Ven. abbreviates Venerable, the title of an archdeacon
first letter of the word
rice is a cereal grain
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A cleric begins by carrying corn around a big room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' looks like the verb joining the priest to the grain, but only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A ventricle is one of the hollow chambers of the heart or brain, so chamber is a direct synonym.

clue.text: In place of wedding feast, a way to serve game

indicators.note: one thing in another is held inside it

blocks.note: Cana in Galilee, where the Gospel of John sets the wedding at which water became wine
taken as written
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Instead of a wedding banquet, guests are offered a game to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In place of' reads as 'instead of', but 'In' is the containment signal and 'place of wedding feast' is the biblical town.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-type card game played with two packs, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: What the unsuccessful might get currently in this place?

definitions.note: the phrase describes the answer, which is an adverb completing 'get'

blocks.note: now means at the present time
here means at this spot

explanation.surface: A wry question about what failures end up with at this moment, in this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works by completing the idiom: people who fail 'get nowhere'.
explanation.definitionFit: To get nowhere is the idiom for making no progress, which is the fate of those who never succeed.

clue.text: South American couple bearing a lot of intense pain

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the word loses its final letter
to bear is to carry, so the outer piece carries another within it

blocks.note: a couple of people, here two names, Pat and Ian
agony is extreme suffering; the final letter goes

explanation.surface: A pair of travellers from South America are suffering badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The couple is two people named Pat and Ian, a liberty Times setters sometimes take; 'a lot of' trims the final Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Patagonia is the southern region of Argentina and Chile, so its native is a South American.

clue.text: Amphibian wife found in trap

indicators.note: something found in another sits inside it

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife
a net is used to trap fish or animals

explanation.surface: A frog-like creature's spouse ends up caught in a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter for wife sits between the second and third letters of the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A newt is a small tailed amphibian related to salamanders, a specific example of the class.

clue.text: Wise director initially hailed in new autobiographical book

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only opening letters are kept
making the letters new means rearranging them into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
first letters of each word

explanation.surface: A sage film director is acclaimed for a new memoir.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words after 'initially' supply a letter. Cider with Rosie (1959) is Laurie Lee's memoir of a childhood in a Cotswold village.
explanation.definitionFit: The book is Laurie Lee's account of his own boyhood, the first part of an autobiographical trilogy.

clue.text: Chemically analyse it in time and degree

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written
rate means extent or degree, as in 'at any rate'

explanation.surface: An instruction to test a substance in the lab, measuring duration and extent.
explanation.walkthrough: The small word goes between the time letter and the degree word, which here join together.
explanation.definitionFit: To titrate is to find a solution's concentration by adding a reagent gradually, a standard chemical analysis technique.

clue.text: Old militia do what a conductor might do

definitions.text: do what a conductor might do
definitions.note: a verb phrase, read as the two words train band

blocks.note: first meaning: a historical company of citizen soldiers

blocks.clueFragment: do what a conductor might do
blocks.note: second meaning: to coach a group of musicians

explanation.surface: A curious comparison between old part-time soldiers and an orchestra's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the answer into two words. Trainbands were citizen militias in 16th and 17th century England, especially London.
explanation.definitionFit: The trained bands were early modern English civic militia companies, and a conductor rehearses and drills musicians.

clue.text: It may remove dirt rapidly at first with hot water

indicators.note: at first points to the very start of a word, so only its opening letter counts

blocks.note: being in hot water and in a scrape both mean being in trouble
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Quick cleaning advice: scrub hard first, then use hot water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot water' looks like a cleaning aid but means trouble; 'with' lets the single letter go after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scraper is a tool for removing mud, paint or grime from a surface, so it may remove dirt.

clue.text: Carelessly lose pay in Pacific island group

indicators.note: something done carelessly ends up jumbled and out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A worker careless with money forfeits their wages on a South Sea island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link to the island group, but it belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Polynesia is the large triangle of islands in the central and southern Pacific Ocean, including Hawaii and Samoa.

clue.text: Aquatic bird priest caught boarding vessel

indicators.note: to board a ship is to step inside it, so the pieces before this word go within the one after

blocks.note: a pan is a cooking vessel
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Old Testament
c. is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cleric is arrested getting onto a ship with a seabird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a kitchen pan; the priest and the cricket letter go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelican is a large water bird with a throat pouch for catching fish, an example of an aquatic bird.

clue.text: Worldly Liberal wearing blue?

indicators.note: something worn by another is covered by it, so this piece goes inside

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
blue means smutty, and earthy humour is crude

explanation.surface: A sophisticated Liberal politician dressed in the colour of the Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the British Conservative colour, so a Liberal in blue looks political; here blue means risqué.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthly means of this world rather than heaven, which is the spiritual contrast that worldly also carries.

clue.text: Earnings right for a new resident

blocks.note: income is money earned
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A newcomer to town claims an entitlement to earned money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earnings right' sounds like a claim to wages, but the abbreviation is simply added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An incomer is someone who has moved into a community from elsewhere, a mainly British usage.

clue.text: Casual workers conserving extremely large places of worship

indicators.note: to conserve is to keep safe inside, so one piece holds another
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only those letters are kept

blocks.note: temps are temporary staff
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Part-time staff protecting huge religious buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely large' reads as 'enormous' describing the buildings, but it asks for the ends of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A temple is a building dedicated to religious worship, so the plural matches places of worship.

clue.text: Reportedly hear military engineers constructing an ancient warship

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so its sound counts

blocks.note: a judge hears or tries a case
the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Army engineers are said to listen while building an old galley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' is the courtroom sense, to try a case. Military engineers are usually RE in crosswords; here it is the longer British Army corps REME.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was a Greek or Roman galley with three banks of oars, used as a fighting ship in antiquity.

clue.text: Small bagpipe group has broken making no sound

a set is a group of things

explanation.walkthrough: 'Has broken' sounds like the instruments failing, but it says the group breaks into the silent word.
explanation.definitionFit: A musette is a small French bagpipe popular in the 17th and 18th centuries, so this is a direct name.

clue.text: Italian citizen’s former nurse disturbed by current directions

three compass points, east, south and east

explanation.definitionFit: A Sienese is a native or inhabitant of Siena, the Tuscan city, so the word names an Italian citizen.

clue.text: Survey originally catching on in period of revival

first letter of the word

clue.text: Cross sequence of letters from tetchy bridegroom

last letters of each word
